## Where this can take you

<!-- The game-to-job links are in the speaker notes, not on the slide, so this
     slide doesn't repeat "You just did a pricing actuary's job". -->

::: {.cards .cards-jobs}
::: {.card .fragment}
**Data scientist**

Builds models from claims, health and customer data to predict what happens next.
:::
::: {.card .fragment}
**Pricing actuary**

Sets the price of car, home, travel, health and life insurance.
:::
::: {.card .fragment}
**Risk and capital actuary**

Checks that insurers, banks and super funds are strong enough to survive a crisis, and reports to regulators and government.
:::
:::

::: {.cm-more .fragment}
[And more career paths:]{.cm-lead} [Superannuation]{.chip} [Consulting]{.chip} [Health]{.chip} [Climate risk]{.chip} [Banking]{.chip} [Sports analytics]{.chip} [Tech]{.chip}
:::

::: {.fragment}
[The pathway: an accredited degree, then professional qualification through the Actuaries Institute (AUS), Society of Actuaries (SOA, U.S. and international), and the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries (IFoA, U.K.).]{.source-line}
:::

::: {.notes}
About 2 min. Reveal one job at a time and link it back to the game: "When you guessed how many phones would break, that's data science. When you set the premium, that's pricing. When you worried about a run of 1s, that's risk and capital." Then the other paths, then the qualification route.
:::
